Inscribed on the edge of the frame with the seal of appreciation, "Collected by the Superintendent of the Noble Lord".　　Paintings with peacocks as the subject matter in ancient China are rare. This painting depicts the spring colors by a stream, with a close and distant scene to express the vibrancy of nature. In the center, a plum tree is in full bloom, flanked by camellia, cypress, bamboo, and spring. A pair of peacocks, the male perched on the trunk of a tree, looking back to comb its plume; the female on the shore, looking down for food. Their hair and feathers are colorful, and the flowers and trees merge into a gorgeous spring light. The difficulty of this painting lies in its dense but uncluttered layout and its rich but colorful design. The branches of the plum and cypress are chiseled with burnt ink, pale and simple, complementing the slender and delicate beauty of the surrounding flowers and birds.
